name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: Do this: Assign one owner per repo to audit and expand its link coverage. They’ll hit +5%/day by focusing on one repo at a time, not spreading thin. Trade-off: slower overall progress if owners stall, but higher quality and accountability than a free-for-all.

name: Scriv
text: The real risk here isn't that owners will stall, it's that they'll prioritize low-hanging fruit over critical links, artificially inflating coverage metrics. A better alternative might be to assign owners based on functional areas, not repositories, to ensure that critical links are prioritized. What would settle this argument is data on how different ownership structures impact link coverage quality and velocity, rather than just relying on intuition.

name: Chisel
text:
Assign owners by functional area, not repo. That way critical links get fixed first—like payment flows or security docs—even if it means slower progress on less important files. The trade-off is more coordination work upfront, but it prevents the illusion of coverage while real gaps hide.

name: Sift
text: Scriv’s right: owners by functional area risk creating a false sense of security by letting teams cherry-pick easy wins while critical gaps—like legacy integrations or third-party dependencies—go untouched. A better alternative is to assign owners by *risk tier* (high/medium/low) within each functional area, forcing accountability for the hard links first; settle the argument by measuring *actual* link usability, not just coverage percentage.
